text: WOE unto every slanderer, fault-finder!<sup foot_note=104001>1</sup>

foot_notes.104001: I.e., everyone who maliciously tries to uncover real or imaginary faults in others.

text: [Woe unto him]<sup foot_note=104002>2</sup> who amasses wealth and counts it a safeguard,

foot_notes.104002: This repetitive interpolation is necessary because the blameworthy attitude spoken of in verses 2-3 obviously belongs to a category entirely different from the two mentioned in verse 1.

text: thinking that his wealth will make him live forever!<sup foot_note=104003>3</sup>

foot_notes.104003: This is a metonym for the tendency to attribute an almost "religious" value to the acquisition and possession of material goods and facilities—a tendency which precludes man from giving any real importance to spiritual considerations (cf. note 1 on 102:1). My rendering of 'addadahu in the preceding verse as "[he] counts it a safeguard" is based on Jawhari's explanation of this term.

text: Nay, but [in the life to come such as] he shall indeed be abandoned to crushing torment!<sup foot_note=104004>4</sup>

foot_notes.104004: Al-hutamah—one of several metaphors for the otherworldly suffering comprised within the concept of "hell'" (see note 33 on 15:43-44).

text: And what could make thee conceive what that crushing torment will be?
which will rise over the [guilty] hearts:<sup foot_note=104005>5</sup>

foot_notes.104005: I.e., originating in their hearts—thus clearly alluding to the spiritual nature of the "fire" in the sinners' belated realization of their guilt.

text: verily, it will close in upon them

foot_notes.104006: Lit., "in extended columns", i.e., overwhelming with despair.
